name: Mixed Neuronal-Glial Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Presence of both neuronal and glial cell components on histopathological examination
MRI showing a well-demarcated cortical or subcortical lesion with cystic and solid components
Focal seizures or epilepsy resistant to medical therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mixed neuronal and glial components with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing may assist in diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal onset seizures with preserved awareness
searchTerms: seizures starting in one area with awareness
focal seizures without loss of consciousness
seizure activity linked to brain dysplasia

common.symptomName: Headache associated with intracranial mass effect
searchTerms: painful head due to mass effect
weakness on one side of body
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased brain pressure

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including depression or anxiety

searchTerms: brain fluid buildup from tumor blockage
water accumulation in brain due to tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction caused by brain lesion

rare.symptomName: Hemorrhage within tumor causing acute neurological deterioration
searchTerms: bleeding inside tumor causing sudden symptoms
tumor hemorrhage leading to neurological decline

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
imaging: MRI showing mixed cystic and solid cortical lesions with contrast enhancement
T2-weighted hyperintense lesions with well-demarcated borders
genetic: BRAF V600E mutation detected in a subset of tumors
Other MAPK pathway alterations may be present
other: Histopathology revealing mixed neuronal and glial cell populations
Immunohistochemistry positive for neuronal markers (NeuN, synaptophysin) and glial markers (GFAP)

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly neuronal tumor with glial component but often with more prominent neuronal atypia
More frequent cystic components and calcifications on imaging
Typically presents with drug-resistant epilepsy in children and young adults
Histology shows specific glioneuronal elements with a characteristic mucinous matrix

redFlags: New onset of focal neurological deficits
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Ellison DW, et al. Mixed neuronal-glial tumors: clinical and molecular features. Brain Pathol. 2019.
